title: Coral assisted evolution research pace
bottleneck: Coral reefs are in near-irreversible die-off — the first tipping point already crossed per the Global Tipping Points report — and assisted evolution to breed heat-tolerant corals is the main hope, but 28 experts warned in 2026 that research is being outpaced by warming. Critical knowledge gaps around the biology of coral heat tolerance hinder progress, and successful interventions need century-long maintenance at large input levels to matter. Restoration today operates at hundreds of square meters against losses of 12,000 square kilometers.
why_it_blocks: Reefs support a quarter of marine species and half a billion people's livelihoods; losing them unravels tropical coastal economies and food systems. If assisted evolution arrives too late, the only remaining lever is emissions cuts that are not happening fast enough.
current_state: The Nature Reviews Biodiversity agenda set nine research priorities to fast-track assisted evolution, and pre-existing heat-tolerant genotypes show promise. But funding and research velocity remain far below what the timeline demands.

sources.title: Coral reef science must adapt for a chance to outpace climate change, say experts
